thread:
oliver: Heads-up: after the adaptive batching heuristic rollout at 09:12, we saw p99 latency jump for small requests (<=32 tokens) and overall throughput drop on rtx-pool-3. Anyone else seeing this?
maya: Yeah noticed it in dashboards. p99 from ~45ms -> ~180ms for tiny requests. Throughput down ~12%.
sam: Timeline: heuristic changed token_budget scaling to be proportional to idle_time and queue_depth (PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/8567). Deployed 09:10.
priya: grabbing flame graphs and perf counters now. posting traces. trace_id=tx-7a9f
priya: Flame snippet: (top 5)
  - op_selector::pick_kernel (31%)
  - cuda_stream_sync (18%)
  - kv_cache::lookup (12%)
  - batch_assembler::dispatch (9%)
  - model_exec::forward (6%)
priya: Interesting: op_selector is taking a lot more time on small sequences. traces show repeated kernel re-selection per request when batch sizes fluctuate.
oliver: Could the adaptive token budget be causing unstable batch composition, so the kernel picker oscillates between small-seq kernel and generic kernel?
maya: I think so. The heuristic reduces token budget aggressively on low-latency targets, producing many very small micro-batches. Those micro-batches trigger different kernel choices and extra setup overhead.
sam: Also saw kv_cache hit ratio drop from 0.92 -> 0.78 on the affected pool during the window. Maybe cold KV entries due to different prefix alignment when batching changes?
priya: Attached a quick repro: run loadgen with --seq-len-dist=short --rps=400 against rtx-pool-3 and toggle heuristic: 
```
./loadgen --targets=endpoint://embed --seq=<=32 --rps=400 --duration=300
# flip heuristic off via /api/heuristics/scale=false
```
priya: Perf counters sample (aggregated 60s):
  dispatch_latency_ms: median 2.1, p95 18.4, p99 162.3
  kernel_selection_ms: median 0.2, p95 12.6, p99 98.1
  kv_hit_ratio: 0.79

maya: Hypothesis: small micro-batches + jitter cause op_selector to re-evaluate kernels per-request rather than per-batch; combined with kv cache prefetch missing, we get extra cuda_stream_syncs.
oliver: Agreed. Quick mitigations?
sam: Options: (1) enforce a minimum token_budget floor for short-seq traffic, (2) prioritize small-seq kernel when seq_len <= 32 to avoid selection churn, (3) add hysteresis to kernel selector so once chosen, stick for N ms unless clear violation.
priya: I pushed a tiny config change to try (1) and (2) on canary: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/changes/8672 (config only, no runtime code). Canary started 09:55.
deploy-bot: deploy started for infra/canary-heuristic-config by priya at 1801295700
priya: Early canary numbers: p99 for small reqs down to ~60ms, throughput recovered ~8%. kv_hit_ratio up to 0.88. kernel_selection_ms p99 down to 24ms.
maya: Good. We should also schedule a follow-up to add selector hysteresis; this mitigation is config-only and may not fully fix oscillation under variable load.
oliver: Agreed—file an engineering task. Also need a short postmortem note for the rollout channel: summarize cause (heuristic induced micro-batching -> kernel churn + kv colding) and mitigation (min token_budget + small-kernel bias).
sam: Filing task: INFRA-1294 (kernel-selector hysteresis + telemetry). adding owners @maya @oliver.
priya: I'll let canary run for 30m and then promote if stable.
oliver: Thanks. If numbers look good after 30m, we rollback the original PR or keep config patch? prefer config patch for faster rollback.
maya: Agreed. keep config patch and schedule deeper fix for next sprint. :thumbsup:
priya: updating dashboards and will post final status in ~40m.
